links.outcome: Fabricated or misrepresented references in GPT-5 answers to orthopaedic exam questions
links.effect: Hallucinated references in 33% of 88 sampled responses; 50% in incorrect vs 15.9% in correct answers (p=0.001).
links.quote: In the subset of 88 responses, hallucinations occurred in 33% overall, significantly higher in incorrect (50%) than in correct answers (15.9%; p=0.001).

links.outcome: Exam benchmark accuracy versus reference reliability of the model's supporting evidence
links.effect: GPT-5 scored 78.3% (159/203) on the OITE, but one in three answers cited fabricated or misrepresented evidence.
links.quote: GPT-5 appears to exceed previously reported LLM performance on the OITE and achieved accuracy higher than published mean scores for senior trainees, but demonstrated poor reference reliability, with one in three answers citing fabricated or misrepresented evidence.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks an LLM on an orthopaedic examination (OITE), evaluating its accuracy, reasoning concordance, and reference hallucination rates without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
